findings.claim: The normative contract, mirrored to every runtime, cites line numbers in an external repository (memorycard/internal/memory/save.go:287-291, :377-389, :281-286). These will drift silently and no test checks them. The rationale for keeping the hard no-op also became weaker: the save adds no version, so the remaining reason (archived restore, a promote over unchanged content) is less clear to a reader.

The origin-changed row is now a single very long table cell holding several procedural steps (supersede, page patch, chunk tombstoning, manifest exception, N==1 exception). It is hard to scan, and agents following the operator procedure may miss the tombstone step. It also asserts that the next `sync` patches the old page to `superseded`, which depends on propagation behaviour that this docs-only change does not verify.

evidence: Reviewed the full diff of the three changed paths; this is a docs-only change and I ran no code.
The contract row at :150 and the hard no-op paragraph at :158-164 carry the new behavioural claims.
The spec edits match the contract wording and keep the R-ids and the Previously notes.
